_meta.purpose: Story micro-game DEFINITIONS, keyed by id. Renderers live in battle.html (StoryMiniGames); these are the tunable numbers the maintainer owns (rounds, tell odds, prompts, win/lose flavour). Attach a game to a scene via data/story/interactions.json (act-level) or via a STORY_BATTLE_INTERRUPTS challenge (battle-level). A micro-game is a SPICE, never a gate: losing never blocks progress. type ∈ 'rps' | 'tell' | 'memory' | 'riddle' | 'spot' | 'cipher' | 'craft'. DESIGN LAW: a signature is high interactivity, little/no mechanical effect — never a battle-MECHANIC change (softenBattle is deprecated/unused). Sanctioned effects: gold / item / flag / giftPokemon, and the RARE skipBattle (pacifist/ransom 'no fight' route). Balance numbers (gold, gift species) are maintainer-owned.

schema.rps: { type:'rps', rounds:int(best-of), tell:0..1(chance CPU plays tellThrow), tellThrow:0|1|2(rock|paper|scissors), title, prompt, winLine, loseLine, drawLine }
schema.tell: { type:'tell', title, tell:'NPC tell line', options:[{label, reply:[...]}], answer:int(correct index), winLine, loseLine }
schema.memory: { type:'memory', length:int, symbols:[emoji...], title, winLine, loseLine }
schema.riddle: { type:'riddle', title, intro:[lines], steps:[{ q, options:[{label, reply:[...]}], answer:int }], passN:int(default=all steps), winLine, loseLine }
schema.spot: { type:'spot', title, prompt, items:[{label, reply:[...]}|str], answer:int(the 'off' one), winLine, loseLine }
schema.cipher: { type:'cipher', title, clue, symbols:[str...], length:int, answer:[idx...], attempts:int(default 3), wrongLine, winLine, loseLine }
schema.craft: { type:'craft', title, gatherPrompt, ingredients:[str...], correct:[idx...], stepsPrompt, steps:[str...], stepOrder:[idx...], winLine, loseLine }

rps_route_punk.title: Rock · Paper · Scissors
rps_route_punk.prompt: "Beat me two outta three and you walk. Lose, and we battle. Throw."
rps_route_punk.winLine: He spits, grins, and waves you past. No battle today.
rps_route_punk.loseLine: "Heh. Then we do this the hard way."

tell_rocket_grunt.title: Read the Tell
tell_rocket_grunt.tell: The grunt's eyes flick left toward the warehouse door before he answers. "Boss ain't here. Nothin' to see."

options.label: "Then you won't mind me checking that door."
reply: He freezes. You called it — he was guarding it.
"...Fine. But you didn't hear it from me."

options.label: "Sure. I'll be on my way."
reply: He relaxes. You let the lead slip.

options.label: "Where's your boss, really?"
reply: "Like I'd tell you," he sneers. The moment's gone.

memory_hypno_trance.title: Hold the Pattern
memory_hypno_trance.winLine: The pendulum swings — and you hold your mind together. The trance breaks.
memory_hypno_trance.loseLine: The lights blur. For a moment you forget where you are...

main_song_memory.title: The Song You Already Know
main_song_memory.winLine: You hum it back before it plays — note for note, right to the end. Your own voice surprises you, like singing a duet with yourself.
main_song_memory.loseLine: You reach for the next note and it isn't there. The song knows itself better than you do.

main_dex_spot.title: The Entry That Wasn't There
main_dex_spot.prompt: The Pokédex page for your starter. One line surfaced while you were looking. Which sentence is in your handwriting?

items.label: Habitat: temperate forests and the edges of towns.
reply: Standard issue. Printed. Not yours.

items.label: Known for unwavering loyalty to a chosen trainer.
reply: Boilerplate. The Dex says it about everything.

items.label: You'll do this again. You always do this again.
reply: There. That slant. The way you cross your sevens.
You have never written in your Pokédex. You'd remember writing that — and that's exactly the thing that's been getting taken.

items.label: Evolves through sustained companionship and training.
reply: Printed. Dry. Theirs.

main_dex_spot.winLine: You spotted it. You wish you hadn't.
main_dex_spot.loseLine: You scan past it twice. Something was right there. You felt it leave.

main_first_riddle.title: Tell The First We Said Hi
intro: The wind takes the stranger before you can ask. But the name sits down in you like you've said it before.

steps.q: When the wind says 'The First,' who does the name fit?

options.label: A champion who came before me.
reply: Maybe. But the certainty in you isn't about a stranger.

options.label: Myself — in another life.
reply: The name sits down like you've worn it. On a peak just like this one. In your own voice, to someone smaller than you.

options.label: Someone I'm supposed to become.
reply: Warmer. The tense is wrong, but the dread is right.

main_first_riddle.winLine: You don't have proof. You have the cold certainty that you've answered this before.
main_first_riddle.loseLine: You let the name go unanswered. It waits. It can afford to.

main_count_cipher.title: The Plate Reads A Number
main_count_cipher.clue: The nameplate beside the figure shows your name — and a number at the end you don't remember entering. Key in the count you see: 0 0 1.
main_count_cipher.wrongLine: Your hand shakes. That isn't the number. Look again.
main_count_cipher.winLine: You key it in yourself. Run 001. The count is a thing you just helped keep — and that's the part that goes cold in you.
main_count_cipher.loseLine: You can't make your hand write it. Some numbers you refuse to inscribe, even when they're already true.

tell_rocket_donated.title: Read the Old Man
tell_rocket_donated.tell: The retired worker holds out the list of DONATED TEST SUBJECTS. 'They called it donation,' he says. 'On the forms. I typed the forms.' He isn't crying. He's waiting for something.

options.label: "You want forgiveness."
reply: 'No,' he says. 'Forgiveness is for people who get to stop. I don't.'

options.label: "You want a witness."
reply: He nods, once, and an ounce of the weight goes off him. 'Somebody besides me has read it now. That's all I came up this road for.'

options.label: "You want me to act on it."
reply: 'Maybe you will. Maybe you can't. That was never the part I needed from you.'

tell_rocket_donated.winLine: You read what he came for. He hands you the list and walks down the road lighter than he's walked in years.
tell_rocket_donated.loseLine: You misread the asking. He folds the list away again, alone with it, and thanks you anyway — which is worse.

riddle_magma_arithmetic.title: The Arithmetic of Mercy
intro: The geologist shoves the depth charts at you, talking faster than he can breathe. 'They did the arithmetic,' he rasps, 'and it agreed with them.'
He needs you to find where the arithmetic lies before his lungs finish the job.

steps.q: Where does Magma's 'mercy' math actually break?

options.label: The numbers are wrong — the chamber won't ignite.
reply: 'No,' he says. 'The numbers are right. That's the whole horror of it.'

options.label: It counts the land and never once counts the people on it.
reply: He laughs, or sobs — hard to tell, this dry. 'There. They did the math a thousand times. Never once on the people.'

options.label: Mercy can't be put in an equation at all.
reply: 'A comfort,' he wheezes. 'But they'd only say you didn't run the numbers hard enough.'

riddle_magma_arithmetic.winLine: You found the missing term. He grips your sleeve like you've handed a piece of his mind back to him.
riddle_magma_arithmetic.loseLine: For a second the arithmetic closes over you, whole and pitiless. You step back from it, shaken at how nearly it held.

tell_aqua_fisherman.title: The Emptied Man
tell_aqua_fisherman.tell: The fisherman stands at the end of the empty mooring, rope still in his hands. 'They left me the rope,' he says. 'So I'd have something to hold.' The tide comes in over his boots. He doesn't step back.

options.label: "Let me help you get a boat back."
reply: He shakes his head, slow. 'It was never the boat.' You've answered a question he didn't ask.

options.label: Say nothing. Step into the tide and stand with him.
reply: You step into the cold beside him and don't step back. After a long while he nods, once. It was the only thing that fit the size of it.

options.label: "It's not your fault."
reply: 'I know,' he says, and the knowing never reaches his hands. The words slide off him like the tide off the rope.

tell_aqua_fisherman.winLine: You read that he needed company, not a fix. Neither of you steps back from the water for a while.
tell_aqua_fisherman.loseLine: You reached for a solution. He needed a witness. The moment closes over like water.

memory_galactic_wall.title: Before They're Filed
memory_galactic_wall.winLine: You hold their faces in order — five Galactic tried to stamp CLOSED ACCOUNT. The wall doesn't get them for free. Not from you.
memory_galactic_wall.loseLine: The faces blur under the clean new flyers before you can fix them. Filed, not found. You couldn't hold them all.

spot_plasma_flyer.title: Who Told You
spot_plasma_flyer.prompt: WHO TOLD YOU THEY WANTED TO BE YOURS? The flyer is on every billboard. Find what the question is hiding.

items.label: The blue is Plasma's exact brand blue.
reply: True. But a colour isn't the tell.

items.label: Small print, bottom edge — sponsored by a foundation with Ghetsis's name on the masthead.
reply: There. The man asking who told you owns the press that prints the asking.
He doesn't need you to put the ball down. He just needs you to keep holding the question.

items.label: The font is expensive.
reply: It is. So is everything they do. Not the tell.

items.label: There's no answer printed anywhere on it.
reply: Of course not — the question was never meant to be answered. Keep looking for who profits from the asking.

spot_plasma_flyer.winLine: You found the masthead. The doubt has an owner now, and an address.
spot_plasma_flyer.loseLine: You read the question and skipped the small print. It keeps doing its quiet work on you a while longer.

tell_flare_scientist.title: Why He's Shaking
tell_flare_scientist.tell: The Flare scientist presses the Ultimate Weapon's design into your hands. Your name is on the recipient list, near the top. He's shaking. 'Now you understand,' he says, 'why I am shaking.'

options.label: "Because you'll be killed for leaking this."
reply: 'No,' he says. 'I'm already dead in every way that frightens me.'

options.label: "Because it's so much worse when they want you to live."
reply: He comes undone, nodding. 'You're on the list of the saved. So am I. We're exactly the sort this is built to spare. That's the obscenity of it.'

options.label: "Because the weapon actually works."
reply: 'It works. But that isn't the part that has my hands like this.'

tell_flare_scientist.winLine: You named the horror he couldn't. He stops shaking, a little — being understood is its own small, terrible mercy.
tell_flare_scientist.loseLine: You missed the shape of his terror. He looks at you like one more person who didn't get it, and never will.

tell_skull_guzma.title: The Booth
tell_skull_guzma.tell: Guzma. Alone in the karaoke booth, the song paused mid-lyric, looking at a printed photo from before. He hasn't seen you. The big bad of the region, and a picture, and a song he isn't singing.

options.label: Step in. Tell him you see him.
reply: He startles, and the bravado slams back up like a shutter. Whatever was open in his face is gone, and it's your fault it's gone.

options.label: Let him have the booth. Walk on.
reply: You don't make him see you. Some men you let have their booth. You've witnessed enough today — he doesn't need to know you witnessed this.

options.label: Get a photo of the moment.
reply: The thought alone shames you. This isn't content. You put the idea down where you found it.

tell_skull_guzma.winLine: You read that being seen would cost him more than it gave. You leave him his one unwatched minute.
tell_skull_guzma.loseLine: You misjudged the moment. The shutter comes down. The big bad is big and bad again — and lonelier for it.

spot_yell_posters.title: The Crack in the Wall
spot_yell_posters.prompt: Every bus shelter wallpapered with Marnie's face, crossed out in red — a campaign budget's worth of hate. Find the crack in the machine.

items.label: A shelter where the marker bled through to the back.
reply: Sloppy. But not the tell.

items.label: One poster, third row, where her face isn't crossed out at all.
reply: A miss. A single uncrossed face in a town of crossed ones.
Somebody wheat-pasted this for a paycheck and hesitated on exactly one. There's a person inside the machine. People can be reached.

items.label: The hashtag printed under every one.
reply: The brand's, yes — but brands don't hesitate. People do. Look again.

items.label: The record-label logo in the corner.
reply: Whose money it is. Not whose hands. Keep looking for the hands.

spot_yell_posters.winLine: You found the one she's not crossed out on. A crack. You stop watching the crowd and start watching who pays for it.
spot_yell_posters.loseLine: You saw only the crowd. The budget behind it stays invisible, and effective, a while longer.

spot_macro_obituary.title: Read Every Page
spot_macro_obituary.prompt: The retired trainer's career obituary, framed in brand colours. 'Read it,' she says. Find the word that isn't true.

items.label: "Beloved by fans across the region."
reply: Probably true, even. Not the lie.

items.label: "Retired voluntarily."
reply: 'That one,' she says when you point. 'I didn't write it. I signed something once that let them write it.'
'Read every page next time. There's always a page near the back about how you'll be remembered. That's the page that costs you.'

items.label: "A celebrated career."
reply: Theirs to inflate. Not the load-bearing lie.

items.label: The dates of her championship run.
reply: Accurate. The facts are never the lie. The framing is.

spot_macro_obituary.winLine: You found the word. 'Voluntarily.' She nods like you passed something she's stopped expecting people to pass.
spot_macro_obituary.loseLine: You read the brand's version and believed it for a second. That second is exactly how it works.

craft_star_rota.title: The Kitchen Rota
craft_star_rota.gatherPrompt: The twelve-year-old runs the kitchen for fifteen kids. Three are out sick today. Pick the cooks who can actually cover tonight.
ingredients: The one who can only really make rice
The careful one who reads the recipe twice
The youngest — too small to reach the stove
craft_star_rota.stepsPrompt: Now set the order so nobody's swamped: who preps, who cooks, who closes.
steps: Careful one preps and reads the recipe aloud
Rice kid plates up and cleans down
craft_star_rota.winLine: It works — not because you did it for them, but because you did it with them. The kid watches you treat the problem as real. Penny notices you're not like the other adults.
craft_star_rota.loseLine: Your plan doesn't fit their kitchen. The kid quietly reworks it after you've gone — the way they rework everything an adult hands them.

riddle_cubone_page.title: The Weight
intro: The diary page, in a child's careful hand: 'Mom says when she goes I have to wear hers so I'll remember the weight.'
The next page is torn out — clean, and recent.

steps.q: It was torn by someone who couldn't bear it. Couldn't bear what?

options.label: What the next page said.
reply: Maybe. A thing too heavy to keep where you'd read it again.

options.label: That the next page stopped.
reply: Maybe. An unfinished sentence is its own kind of unbearable.

options.label: You can't tell which is worse — and that's the weight.
reply: Yes. The not-knowing is the inheritance. That's what 'remember the weight' was always going to mean.

riddle_cubone_page.winLine: You understand the weight now. You leave the page where it is. It isn't yours to carry. Not yet.
riddle_cubone_page.loseLine: The meaning slips just past you. You leave the page, unsure what you almost understood.

spot_yamask_faceless.title: Who Isn't Quite Right
spot_yamask_faceless.prompt: A man missing his face just asked you for directions and walked off, polite. Everyone else is very carefully having a different conversation. Look again — who else here isn't quite right?

items.label: The trucker reading a newspaper upside down.
reply: Distracted, maybe. But he has a face. Look at who's being not-looked-at.

items.label: The woman at the vending machine — smooth, with eyes set where a face would keep them.
reply: There. And the way the others angle away from her mid-sentence, agreeing without a word not to have noticed.
The faceless don't hide. We hide them, by looking somewhere else.

items.label: The kid kicking a can by the pumps.
reply: Just a kid. Has a face, has a scowl. Not the one.

items.label: The clerk behind the counter.
reply: Bored. Human. Faced. Not the one.

spot_yamask_faceless.winLine: You let yourself see the one everyone agreed not to. It's the only courtesy the faceless ever get.
spot_yamask_faceless.loseLine: You look where everyone else is looking — which is to say, away. The smooth one stays unseen.

memory_hypno_year.title: The Year They Lost
memory_hypno_year.winLine: You hold the shape of a whole year — the one the nap tucked away so neatly the child never noticed the bed had been disturbed. You held what they couldn't.
memory_hypno_year.loseLine: The year slips through your fingers too, smooth and complete, like it was never there. Now you understand how gentle the taking is.

spot_phantump_register.title: The Handwriting Matches Yours
spot_phantump_register.prompt: The swollen notebook — a register of names in many hands, decades deep. The last entry is dated yesterday. Find it.

items.label: A name in faded brown ink, halfway down.
reply: Old. Decades old. Not yesterday's.

items.label: The last line — fresh ink, dated yesterday, in handwriting that's yours.
reply: Not similar. Yours. The exact slant, the way you cross your sevens.
You didn't write it. You check twice, and being sure is so much worse than doubting.

items.label: A name crossed out near the top.
reply: Someone changed their mind once. Not the one.

items.label: A blank line at the very end.
reply: Waiting — but empty. The entry you want is already filled, in your hand.

spot_phantump_register.winLine: You find your own hand on a page you never wrote. You do not add to the list. You're not certain it needs you to.
spot_phantump_register.loseLine: You can't pick it out among the years of names. Maybe that's the mercy. You don't add to the list either way.

tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.title: Didn't Feel Right
tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.tell: The thrift-shop costume, returned three times by three kids who each said it 'didn't feel right.' The shopkeeper shrugs. 'Kids are particular.'

options.label: "Kids are particular. Find it a buyer."
reply: The shopkeeper nods, relieved to move it along. The costume hangs there, the wrong shape, waiting.

options.label: Take it down and try it on yourself.
reply: You don't, in the end. Something about the idea makes your skin go cold. You set it back on the hook.

options.label: Press: why did all three say the exact same words?
reply: The shopkeeper hesitates, then, lower: 'One of 'em said it was wearing her. Not the other way round.'
Three kids, the same costume returning like a tide. Exactly the right shape for something that isn't a child at all.

tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.winLine: You pressed, and the shape of it came clear. It isn't a costume kids keep rejecting. It's a thing trying on children.
tell_mimikyu_shopkeeper.loseLine: You let it lie. The costume keeps its hook, and its patience, and its wrong shape.

spot_drifloon_board.title: The Board Is Full
spot_drifloon_board.prompt: The 'lost balloons' board — a kid's name and a date on every slip, and the board is full. Find what's actually wrong with it.

items.label: The slips are layered over slips, years deep.
reply: A lot of them, yes. But quantity isn't the tell.

items.label: The dates are weekly — regular as a bus schedule, no gaps, no missed weeks.
reply: A schedule, not a run of accidents. Accidents don't keep appointments.
Somebody adds to this board every week and has never once gotten to take a slip down.

items.label: Some of the names are misspelled.
reply: Grief spells badly sometimes. Not the tell.

items.label: The newest slip is this week's.
reply: It is — and next week's isn't pinned yet, but it will be. That's the horror, not the tell itself.

spot_drifloon_board.winLine: You see it: a schedule wearing the costume of bad luck. The most recent date is this week. You don't look for next week's.
spot_drifloon_board.loseLine: You read it as a sad coincidence, the way you're meant to. The board fills on schedule regardless.

tell_parasect_break.title: Who's Steering
tell_parasect_break.tell: The Paras walks a perfect figure-eight — over, across, around — and won't stop, and won't eat, and the mushroom on its back is humming. Watch closely before you decide what you're seeing.

options.label: It's training — drilling a route.
reply: A Paras doesn't drill. And it would have broken off to investigate you. This one didn't.

options.label: The bug's choosing to. It finds the loop restful.
reply: Look at the groove worn into the dirt. That isn't a choice. That's a thing done past the point of choosing.

options.label: The mushroom is steering. The bug's opinion stopped being collected a while ago.
reply: The hum gives it away — the same note as a pendulum, a chair, the things that hum when something else is driving.
A figure-eight is infinity laid flat. The bug walks it because the mushroom can, and the bug can't anymore.

tell_parasect_break.winLine: You read who's actually steering. You step around the groove without breaking it — breaking it would cost the bug, and the bug has lost enough.
tell_parasect_break.loseLine: You can't quite see it. The wrongness stays just under the surface, humming. You walk on unsettled, not knowing why.

memory_mewtwo_future.title: Three Seconds Early
memory_mewtwo_future.winLine: You hold the sequence the afterimage leaked — the next three seconds, in order, before they happen. Something nearby is cracking the future, and for a moment you read the crack.
memory_mewtwo_future.loseLine: The leaked moment scatters before you can fix it. Time re-seats itself. To everyone else it was always ordinary; to you, for three seconds, it wasn't.

tell_plasma_knights.title: The Reluctant Bridge
tell_plasma_knights.tell: The two Plasma knights block the bridge in real plate armor, and they do not want to. 'Sorry,' one says before you've moved. 'Forgive us. We don't—' There's a way past that isn't through. Find it.

options.label: "You don't have to do this. Stand aside."
reply: They look at each other. The doctrine says release; the king says war; you've offered the third thing nobody offered them.
Armor creaking, they step aside. '...Go,' one whispers. 'Before we remember we were told to stop you.'

options.label: "Then fight me and get it over with."
reply: They flinch — and obey, because being told to fight is the one instruction they were ever taught to follow.

options.label: "Your apologies don't free anyone."
reply: The words land like a slap. Shame curdles into resolve. They raise their gloves.

tell_plasma_knights.winLine: You gave them the exit their king never would. They let you pass. No battle today.
tell_plasma_knights.loseLine: They square up, reluctant and immovable. The hard way, then.

rps_skull_standoff.title: Saving Face
rps_skull_standoff.prompt: 'Yo yo yo—' The two Skull grunts can't afford to lose face and can't afford to lose. One jabs a finger at you. 'Beat us at THIS, you walk. Lose, we throw down. THROW!'
rps_skull_standoff.winLine: They whoop like they planned it, slap your shoulder too hard, and wave you past. Saving face is the only currency they've got — you let them keep it. No battle.
rps_skull_standoff.loseLine: 'HAH! Now we GOTTA fight — that's the rules!' They're almost relieved.
